pattern.crimePattern: ruined trader pulls a stack of sacks down on the wholesaler who sold her expired re-bagged sugar
pattern.notes: Fictional wholesaler and trader. Expired and re-bagged sugar has been a recurring public-health story in Kenya; no real case, company or official is depicted. The illness of Sarah's customers is described only as "fell ill".

ob.text: A market helper reports his employer, sugar wholesaler Joshua Obura (58), found under a collapsed stack of 50 kg sugar sacks in his lock-up store at Kibuye market at 12:05. The helper had been out delivering.

people.name: Joshua Obura
people.bio: Twenty-five years selling sugar by the sack at Kibuye. Known for a loud laugh and a hard bargain.

facts.text: Joshua Obura, sugar wholesaler, was found under a collapsed stack of 50 kg sacks in his store at Kibuye market at 12:05.
Twelve 50 kg sacks collapsed across Joshua by his counter.
The top three sacks of the fallen stack have fresh tears in the weave, as if hooked and pulled from above.
A sack by the counter carries a tag: "OPOLOT GENERAL SHOP — BUSIA — RETURNED".
Inside the outer "Kenyan Sugar" sack is an inner imported bag printed "Best before", with a date two years past.
Joshua's back room: bales of new empty sacks printed "Kenyan Sugar", a sack-sewing machine, and a pile of torn-open imported bags.
Rebecca: at 11:40 the store's shutter was half down, which Joshua never does on a Sunday. She called; nobody answered. She bought next door.
Lilian: Yusuf served her and her sister at his counter from 11:00 to 12:00. "He weighed everything twice. He always does."
Market master's receipt: Joshua's daily fee collected at 11:10. Hassan stayed to chat; Joshua was "laughing as usual".
Hassan's next receipts are in the shoe section: 11:18, 11:26, 11:35.
Ben's delivery notes: drops in Manyatta signed by customers at 11:08, 11:20 and 11:50. He was back at 12:05 and found him.
Diana: in October she seized Sarah Opolot's sugar in Busia after customers fell ill. She traced it to "a Kisumu wholesaler" but couldn't name him yet.
Diana: Sarah was held for two nights, released without charge, and lost her shop.
Diana was at the Sunday service at her church in Milimani from 10:00 to 12:30.
Bus passenger list: "S. OPOLOT — Busia–Kisumu — departed 08:30 — arrived 11:00".
Sarah's receipt: 40 bags from Obura Sugar Stores, paid in full in cash on 9 October.
Stall register: Sarah Opolot has no stall at Kibuye and has never paid a fee there.
From Sarah's bag: a steel sack hook, sugar crystals stuck in the grease of its handle.
Fingerprints taken from Sarah Opolot in detention.
Autopsy: crush asphyxia under heavy weight. He couldn't breathe under the sacks.
Autopsy: bruises on both wrists from a hard grip, made minutes before the crush.
Autopsy: death between 11:00 and 12:30.
Autopsy: no head injury, and a heart in good condition for his age. Nothing in his stomach but tea.
Lab: Sarah Opolot's fingerprints are on the hook's handle, in the grease and sugar.
Lab: sack fibres on the hook's tip match the torn weave of the top three sacks.
Sarah: "I came on the afternoon bus. I only got to Kisumu at two."
Sarah: "That man poisoned my customers."
Sarah admits she went to Joshua's store at about 11:15 with a sack of his sugar "so he could see it".
Ben: "I was delivering in Manyatta."
Ben: "He paid me badly. Everyone knows it. I wouldn't kill him for that."
Ben: Joshua sewed new sacks in the back room on Saturday nights. "Mzee said not to ask."
Yusuf: "I was at my counter all morning."
Yusuf: "I told him five years ago: one day that re-sacking will kill somebody."

interrogations.intro: Sarah sits very straight on the bench outside the market master's office, her cloth bag on her knees. "I heard. I won't pretend to cry."

topics.reply: Yes, that is my tag. I sent it back to him weeks ago. He never answered.
Two nights in a cell with my customers' children crying outside. My shop is gone. He sold me poison and called it sugar.

interrogations.intro: Ben sits on the edge of the handcart, sugar dust on his arms, not looking at the store. "I found him. I pulled two sacks off before I understood."

topics.reply: He paid me badly. Everyone knows it. I wouldn't kill him for that.
Saturday nights he sewed new sacks in there. Mzee said not to ask. So I didn't ask.

interrogations.intro: Yusuf keeps weighing sugar into kilo bags as you talk. "His business is his business. I sell sugar."

topics.reply: I told him five years ago: one day that re-sacking will kill somebody. He laughed. He always laughed.

interrogations.intro: Hassan flips his receipt book open to the morning. "I took his fee at ten past eleven. He was laughing."

topics.reply: Opolot? No stall here, never. Let me check the register. ...No. Nothing.

interrogations.intro: Diana comes straight from church, Bible still in her hand. She looks at the inner bag for a long time. "That's the sugar. That's the one."

topics.reply: A sewing machine and new sacks. I'll need that room sealed, Detective.

contradictions.reaction: She closes her eyes. "...I came in the morning. I brought him his rotten sugar so he could see it. He laughed. I left."

prosecutor.pass: Laughing with the market master at ten past eleven, shutter down at twenty to twelve. That's the window.
fail: He paid his fee at 11:10. He was alive then.
The shutter was down at 11:40 and nobody answered. Narrow it from that side too.

prosecutor.pass: In Kisumu from eleven, in his store at quarter past, and her prints in the grease of that hook. Charge her.
fail: The helper was getting signatures in Manyatta. Look again.
Yusuf was weighing sugar for customers all morning. Who came from Busia?

prosecutor.pass: Torn sacks at the top, grip marks on his wrists, and a hook in her bag. It didn't fall. Yes.
fail: Sacks don't tear themselves at the top. Read the stack again.
Crush asphyxia. Nothing hit his head.

prosecutor.pass: Charge her. And Amani: make sure Diana gets the back room. Somebody has to answer for that sugar too.
fail: She paid him in full. Read her receipt.
She has no stall here. What did she lose?

timeOfDeath.note: The act window: alive paying his fee at 11:10, shutter down and silent at 11:40. The autopsy allows 11:00–12:30.

proof.concludes: Joshua paid his fee and laughed with the market master at 11:10. At 11:40 his shutter was half down and he didn't answer. He died between 11:10 and 11:40.
Joshua was re-bagging expired imported sugar as "Kenyan Sugar". That is the sugar Diana seized from Sarah's shop in Busia after her customers fell ill.

Sarah wasn't on the afternoon bus: she arrived at 11:00 and was in the store at about 11:15. The stack was hooked and pulled from the top, he was gripped first, and the hook in her bag carries her prints. Sarah Opolot killed Joshua by pulling a stack of sacks down on him, because his expired sugar had cost her everything.

eliminations.why: He was alive and laughing at 11:10.
At 11:40 his shutter was already down and he didn't answer.
Ben found him at 12:05; he was silent at 11:40.
Ben was getting delivery notes signed in Manyatta from 11:08 to 11:50.
Yusuf was serving customers at his own counter from 11:00 to 12:00.
Hassan was stamping receipts in the shoe section at 11:18, 11:26 and 11:35.
Diana was at the Sunday service in Milimani.
The top sacks were hooked and pulled, and he was gripped minutes before.
His heart was sound; he died of the weight.
He died of crush asphyxia, with only tea in his stomach.
That rivalry is Yusuf's, and Yusuf was at his counter.
That grievance is Ben's, and Ben was in Manyatta.
Sarah paid for every bag in full, in cash.
Sarah has no stall at Kibuye.

reconstruction.text: In October Joshua sells Sarah 40 sacks of "Kenyan" sugar for her shop in Busia: expired imported sugar, re-bagged in his back room.
Her customers fall ill. The county seizes her stock; she spends two nights in a cell and loses the shop.
Sunday. She takes the 08:30 bus and arrives at 11:00 with one of his sacks. At 11:10 Joshua pays his market fee, laughing.
About 11:15. She shows him the inner bag. He laughs and tells her to sell it to pigs. She grabs his wrists. When he turns to serve the counter she hooks the top of the stack and pulls.
She pulls the shutter half down and walks into the Sunday crowd with the hook in her bag. At 11:40 Rebecca calls through the shutter. Nobody answers.

clockPlan.note: Detain Sarah once the bus list breaks her story; the hook comes from her bag and her prints are taken in detention. Prints take 6 h. The fibre test is optional.

tier1.line: One fact sets the earliest time. Another sets the latest. Find both.

tier2.line: A fee stamped at 11:10. A shutter down at 11:40.

tier2.line: Tears in the top sacks, and grip bruises on his wrists.

tier2.line: Expired sugar in a new bag, and a shop in Busia that lost everything.

ui.beatNotes: Narrow from both sides. The single WHEN blank teaches the habit the timeline strip will build on: one fact sets the earliest time (the fee receipt), one sets the latest (the shutter). On the rail the two pins shade the window between them.
